instructions: Cut the roots and dark green tops off the leeks. Halve them lengthwise, rinse well between the layers, then slice them thinly.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1/2 inch pieces. Dice the onion, peel and slice 2 of the carrots, and slice the garlic.
Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the leeks and carrots and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the leeks are soft.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, the salt and the pepper and stir. Add the broth and the bay leaf and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Cover, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 18 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Take out the bay leaf.
Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley. Taste the soup. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle it into bowls. Drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle with the parsley.
To pack it, let it cool, then keep it in a container in the fridge for up to 4 days, or freeze it for up to 3 months. Reheat it over medium-low heat with a splash of water.
method_notes: Neither version had enough ratings, so this is a fallback; the lead is Spain on a Fork (5 stars from 1 vote, visible rating). Recipes from Europe had no rating. Both agree on leeks, potatoes, onion and carrot softened in olive oil, then simmered about 20 minutes in broth. The lead adds garlic and a bay leaf and uses vegetable broth, which I kept so the dish is vegetarian; the other uses chicken stock. I used 3 garlic cloves and kept the vegetables in pieces.
